history_of_present_illness: The rash started 3 days prior on the trunk, spreading to extremities and mucosal membranes (lips, oral mucosa, conjunctivae, genital mucosa), accompanied by a productive cough with whitish sputum (started 1 day before the rash), sore throat, and dysuria for 2 days. Two months earlier, she was diagnosed with HIV, hospitalized with cryptococcal meningitis, treated with oral fluconazole, and 1 month prior, started on antiretroviral treatment (stavudine, lamivudine, nevirapine) and co-trimoxazole prophylaxis.
exposure_and_epidemiology: Patient is HIV positive and started co-trimoxazole and antiretroviral triple therapy (d4T, 3TC, NVP) within the past month.
vitals: Temperature 37.7°C (99.9°F), blood pressure 120/68 mmHg, pulse 90 bpm, respiratory rate 24 breath cycles per minute.
physical_exam: Generalized, non-itchy maculopapular rash involving the skin and mucous membranes but sparing the palms and soles, bilateral conjunctivitis, eyelids and lips covered with haemorrhagic crusts, swollen lips making talking and eating difficult and painful, and a clear chest.
labs_and_diagnostics: Blood cultures and a rapid malaria test were negative.
differential_diagnosis: Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS)/toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN) caused by drugs is the most important diagnosis, while staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome, toxic shock syndrome, exfoliative dermatitis, autoimmune bullous diseases, and acute paraneoplastic pemphigus should be considered.
management_and_clinical_course: Antiretroviral drugs and co-trimoxazole were stopped on admission; she received IV fluids and a urinary catheter. The patient and her family declined an NG tube. She was given 0.9% normal saline as mouthwash and dexamethasone eye ointment. Fever and cough settled spontaneously, and she was discharged after 10 days in hospital. Later, she was started on a new antiretroviral combination therapy where nevirapine was replaced by efavirenz; co-trimoxazole was not replaced. The new drug combination was tolerated well, and no further rash occurred.
final_diagnosis: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) caused by nevirapine and co-trimoxazole.
